chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'It has reached us that an Umrah in the month of Ramadan equals a Hajj.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That was only regarding a woman to whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had promised [a reward]. So he (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Perform Umrah in the month of Ramadan, so it is for you a Hajj.'

key_terms.حَجَّة: Hajj (major pilgrimage, specifically the one with the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: Does an Umrah in Ramadan equal a full Hajj for everyone?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the specific reward of an Umrah in Ramadan equating to a full Hajj was a special promise made by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to a specific woman, rather than a general, permanent legal ruling for all Muslims. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of 'khas' (specific) versus 'amm' (general) in hadith, emphasizing that while the general virtue of Ramadan Umrah remains, the unique equivalence to Hajj was a specific favor (fadilah) granted to that individual. This nuance prevents the conflation of a singular prophetic promise with a universal jurisprudential ruling.
